description: v2.5 (CF-WO-P0-006, animation-first, style-agnostic production architecture). One production profile binds the composable production dimensions for a project/series: visual style, production medium, source media, motion methods, subject types and interaction pattern are SEPARATE dimensions — there is no single `animation_type` enum anywhere in this repo (a record carrying `animation_type` is rejected by additionalProperties). A profile may combine media per subject and per shot (see per_subject_overrides / per_shot_overrides); no scene is required to use the same rendering medium for every character. is_live_action_footage is machine-checkable provenance: it MUST be false for generated subjects (ai-digital-human, ai-digital-creature, 3d-cgi-rigged, 2d-drawn-vector) — a generated digital human is NEVER live-action footage. This is a P0 contract/schema record only; it builds no server, API, backend or database. Captured footage uses visual_style `captured-live-action` and motion method `captured-motion` (motion as captured by the camera, not generated); unmanipulated captured real-animal footage is a valid profile with is_live_action_footage true.

is_live_action_footage.description: True ONLY when the production is real captured footage of real subjects. False for every generated subject (AI digital human/creature, CGI, drawn animation). A generated digital human with this set to true is invalid (see the live-action provenance check in tests/test_schemas.py).

per_shot_overrides.description: Per-shot overrides for camera direction. Camera movement must be motivated by the shot's dramatic intent, never arbitrary; static is a valid deliberate choice.

per_subject_overrides.description: Per-subject overrides: each subject may use its own representation, source media, rendering style and motion methods, independent of the profile defaults and of every other subject.

is_live_action_footage.description: Per-subject provenance: false for any generated subject, even inside a hybrid production.

species.description: Species / kind of creature, e.g. 'African grey parrot'. Needed so articulation can be checked against the subject (a bird never uses human lip movement).

skill_profiles.description: Skill slugs (one optional profile per skill, e.g. explainer-animation) that this production routes through. Each entry is a skill slug such as skill-realistic-person.
